notes: Declared accuracies come from each provider's own product specification, not from DEM2DGED. Always read the per-project metadata of the tile you use.
vertical_le90_m is the declared 90% vertical error used for the 3:1 suitability rule of thumb. RMSEz values are converted with LE90 = 1.645 x RMSEz (normal errors assumed).

Suitability rule of thumb: OK if reference LE90 <= the level's vertical random 90% limit / 3; MARGINAL if <= limit / 2; otherwise TOO_COARSE. This is common practice, not a DGIWG requirement. No open dataset listed here reaches OK for levels 6 and finer; those need surveyed ground control points.
A reference must be independent of the conversion source. Check that your source DEM was not derived from the same lidar survey.

sources.resolution_note: 1 m or 2 m (taken from the dataset id suffix, e.g. -1m)
sources.accuracy_statement: Bare-earth vertical accuracy under 50 cm for lidar-sourced datasets (HRDEM product specification).
sources.horizontal_crs_note: Typically EPSG:3979 (NAD83(CSRS) / Canada Atlas Lambert); varies by dataset.
sources.limits: Partial coverage. Lidar mostly in the south; use the satellite-derived collection in the north (accuracy under 2 m, not suitable for fine levels).

sources.accuracy_statement: QL1/QL2 lidar: RMSEz 10 cm (QL3: 20 cm). 0.17 m is 1.645 x 10 cm and assumes QL2 or better. Check the project metadata.
sources.horizontal_crs_note: UTM zone of the project, NAD83; varies by project.
sources.limits: Coverage is project by project and not complete. Tiles are delivered per project; the clip may need several tiles.

sources.accuracy_statement: Accuracy varies by area and source; not stated here. Use only for coarse levels and read the metadata.
sources.limits: Seamless coverage of the conterminous US, but accuracy is not guaranteed to be better than a fine-level product needs.
